key_insight: In 2D Euler flows, a vortex patch can undergo rigid rotation inside a bounded simply connected domain only if the domain is a centered disk; otherwise, the paper constructs quasi-periodic patch motions in small perturbations of the disk.
engineering_relevance: The result clarifies when boundary geometry preserves or destroys coherent vortex structures, which matters for reduced-order modeling and flow control in confined domains.
method: Use a rotating-frame reformulation of the Euler equations.
Apply harmonic unique continuation and generalized Schwarz reflection across analytic boundary arcs.
Construct quasi-periodic vortex patches perturbatively for domains near the unit disk, for most inner radii b.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rigorous theorem-based analysis and perturbative construction results, rather than numerical experiments or data-driven evaluation.
watch_item: The rigidity result assumes a simply connected domain with real-analytic boundary, so the conclusion may not extend directly to rough or multiply connected geometries.
paper_title: Geometric effects on the persistence of patch structures for 2D Euler equations in simply-connected bounded domains
